metadata.title: Teaching and Learning International Survey (TALIS) 2024 Conceptual Framework (EN)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is a conceptual framework and survey design specification for TALIS 2024 rather than an empirical analysis paper. It describes a two-stage sampling design (schools as primary sampling units; teachers as secondary sampling units) with systematic random school selection and random teacher selection within schools, including stratification within schools where possible. It also specifies that the teacher questionnaire uses a rotated/split design with “missing by design” patterns across questionnaire forms, and it states that data are not imputed in the TALIS 2024 datasets. Because no analysis model is reported here, the framework does not specify which complex survey weights (e.g., student/sampling weights or replicate weights) are applied in estimation; analysts should follow the forthcoming TALIS 2024 technical report and database user guide for the exact weighting and variance estimation variables.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because this is a conceptual framework and survey instrument design document for TALIS 2024, which focuses on questionnaire constructs from teachers and principals rather than cognitive achievement scales that use PVs. Missing data handling is not reported in the sense of an estimation strategy for an empirical model; instead, the document explains that some questionnaire items are missing by design due to the rotated/split design and that the TALIS 2024 datasets do not impute these missing-by-design responses. Therefore, there is no single missing-data handling method (e.g., multiple imputation) to extract from results.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: TALIS 2024 targets teachers and principals in schools providing education at ISCED level 2, and teachers/principals at ISCED level 1 and ISCED level 3 for optional modules. Schools devoted entirely to special needs students and schools exclusively offering adult education are out of scope; substitute and emergency teachers are excluded. The sampling is two-stage: schools are selected with systematic random sampling (probability proportional to size, or equal probability in some cases), and teachers are randomly selected within each school with stratification within schools where possible. The nominal sample is approximately 200 schools per participating country per ISCED level and about 20 teachers per school (all teachers if fewer than 20), yielding a nominal country sample of about 4,000 teachers per ISCED level; the teacher questionnaire uses a rotated/split design with three forms, so many items are missing by design for some teachers.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD TALIS 2024 conceptual framework specifies how TALIS will measure contemporary issues affecting teachers, teaching, and learning, including diversity and equity, educational use of technology (including AI), social and emotional learning, and environmental and sustainability education. It outlines the survey’s target populations (teachers and principals at ISCED 1/2/3, with optional modules), exclusion rules (e.g., schools exclusively for adult education; substitute/emergency teachers), and a two-stage sampling approach (schools then teachers within schools). The document also details instrument design choices: a pilot, field trial, and main survey; cross-cultural questionnaire development principles; and a rotated/split teacher questionnaire with three forms to broaden coverage while limiting respondent burden (with “missing by design” and no imputation in the resulting datasets). No empirical ML models, predictive targets, or performance metrics are reported in this document, so there are no quantitative findings to benchmark.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a non-empirical conceptual framework and survey design document for TALIS 2024, not an analysis paper. It does not report an analytic sample with outcomes, does not train or evaluate any machine learning models, and does not provide PV handling or missing-data handling for an estimation model. Consequently, fields required for empirical ML extraction (e.g., main_findings, ml_techniques, and country-level sample sizes) are not populated because the document’s purpose is to define constructs, indicators, and survey operations rather than to produce predictive results.
